title: portfolio
summary: Live chronological portfolio for current systems, restored originals, and future v2 rebuilds.
whyItMatters: This is the surface that turns the cleaned-up GitHub account into a readable career story instead of a loose repository list.
intent: Keep as the canonical portfolio line and release log for the work that remains public.

title: review-game-core
summary: Concept-layer learning toolkit for study products: TypeScript primitives, workflow contracts, and WF-tested docs.
whyItMatters: This is the strongest signal for current product thinking: it shows reusable abstractions, documentation, testing doctrine, and a clearer point of view about learning tools.
intent: Use as a foundation for consumer-facing study products and keep the docs visible as the system matures.

title: astronomy-future-compute
summary: Interactive astronomy presentation rebuilt in Next.js with live controls, a deployed site, and WF coverage.
whyItMatters: It shows the ability to turn a presentation idea into a usable web product with a clear path through the experience.
intent: Keep as a polished shipped example of presentation-as-product work.

title: About-Me
summary: YAML-to-LaTeX career document pipeline for resumes, CVs, cover letters, portfolio exports, and agent-assisted tailoring.
whyItMatters: It belongs beside the portfolio because it generates the structured career artifacts the public site can eventually expose or reference.
intent: Clean up the fork history, document the reworked architecture, and connect generated artifacts back to the portfolio story.

title: lfx
summary: Go CLI for managing lf themes, icons, and plugins: a small terminal control plane with a clear job.
whyItMatters: It is compact, practical tooling that shows comfort working below the web-app layer.
intent: Keep visible as a focused developer-tool example and improve docs only when the CLI behavior changes.

title: Crime-NY
summary: First-year SE bootcamp map using NYC OpenData, Mapbox, and year-based exploration.
whyItMatters: It is not a flagship data-science claim. It is worth keeping because it quietly points toward later interest in visual workflows, maps, public data, and user-facing exploration tools.
intent: Preserve the restored original and revisit only if a v2 can meaningfully improve the original civic-data vision.

title: dogPark
summary: Datadog-sponsored hackathon prototype around lightweight social and organizational discovery.
whyItMatters: It shows early product collaboration under time pressure, but should be read as a prototype rather than a current bar for craft.
intent: Keep as historical context unless a future rebuild has a sharper product reason.

title: SEI-Trivia
summary: Historical full-stack trivia project spanning Rails and mobile clients.
whyItMatters: It gives context for the early full-stack training period without pretending to be current product work.
intent: Keep as an early learning artifact and only elevate it if a future v2 creates a stronger learning-game angle.
